content.figure_caption: Classification of patients presenting with suspected acute coronary syndrome: from a working to a final diagnosis.

flow_stages.details: If a patient has signs/symptoms suggestive of ACS, perform an ECG within 10 min of first medical contact (FMC). Initial ECG findings guide triage.
Based on available clinical information and ECG findings the working ACS diagnosis is classified as STEMI or NSTE-ACS to allow initial triage and assessment.
Assessment with high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) levels and, as indicated, angiography and/or imaging to help establish mechanism and subtype of myocardial infarction (MI).

Final diagnosis (STEMI, NSTEMI, unstable angina, or non-ACS diagnosis) is based on symptoms, ECG, troponin results, and other tests (imaging and/or angiography). Patients initially assigned STEMI or NSTE-ACS may ultimately receive a final non-ACS diagnosis.

notes: Figure references: Figure 3 from ESC guidelines.
The working diagnosis uses ECG and clinical information; the final diagnosis incorporates troponin and additional testing (imaging/angiography).
